A 69-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with hip and back pain.
The patient has a medical history of obesity, diabetes, depression, anxiety, diverticulosis, constipation, and a surgical repair of his anterior cruciate ligament.
On physical exam, he is found to have an intact motor and sensory function in his lower extremities bilaterally.
He describes the pain as in his buttocks but states that at times it travels down his leg.
He states that it feels electrical and burning in nature.
When he was lifting a heavy object, he suddenly felt pain in his lower back.
No clonus or Babinski sign is appreciated.
His temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 131/82 mmHg, pulse is 82/min, and respirations are 14/min.
An exam of the cranial nerves is intact bilaterally.
He states this weekend he had a barbecue.
